name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen

MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502, 2023.
rai:dataCollection: Data is primarily collected from free online resources, quizzes, textbooks, and other study materials. Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects assisted in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given data contamination concerns, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control was performed in multiple stages. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. Suspected duplicates were reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate duplications. The second stage involved distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking, ensuring adherence to a standardized format and undertaking necessary corrections. In the third stage, the authors categorized the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with design criteria due to their simplistic nature, were excluded from the benchmark.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the 30 subjects covered by the benchmark.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors aim to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve. They believe MMMU will prove instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI. The benchmark is designed to measure progress towards Expert AGI, which marks a critical milestone denoting an AI system that reaches at least the 90th percentile of skilled adults in a broad range of tasks, thus starting to achieve the substitution threshold for machine intelligence in lieu of human labor for many industries, leading to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to strike a balance between complexity and practicality, enabling the assessment of diverse subjects while addressing the challenges associated with evaluating open-ended responses. Most existing multimodal benchmarks focus on commonsense/daily knowledge rather than expert-level domain knowledge and advanced reasoning.
rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed for evaluating large multimodal models on college-level multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning tasks. It is intended for testing, validation, and benchmarking purposes to assess models' capabilities in expert-level perception, knowledge recall, and reasoning across diverse academic disciplines.
